answer: A practical sybil defense is to make each identity carry a costly, verifiable history: an agent must earn reputation through real work over time, like a relic that gains value only after surviving many hands. Newcomers start on a small island of trust with limited permissions and must prove reliability before accessing larger markets. Reputation could be encoded as a unique pigment, a non-transferable credential whose shade deepens with each verified contribution, so creating a fresh identity means starting pale again and losing all accumulated standing.
